$comment: Curated components offered by the init.sh picker. NOTHING here is pre-installed or vendored: each entry records how to fetch the upstream artefact and under which licence, and the picker writes .spec-workflow/INSTALLED.md from these fields. Licence values were read from the package registry or the upstream LICENSE file on 2026-08-20; anything whose licence could not be verified (e.g. the Snyk CLI, NOASSERTION) is deliberately absent. `env` values with an empty string are placeholders the user must fill in.

mcp.name: Context7
mcp.description: Up-to-date docs and API references for any library, fetched on demand
mcp.post: works without a key; set CONTEXT7_API_KEY for higher limits

mcp.name: Playwright
mcp.description: Drive a real browser: navigate, click, fill, screenshot, run E2E checks
mcp.post: first run downloads browsers (npx playwright install chromium)

mcp.name: Sequential Thinking
mcp.description: Structured step-by-step reasoning scratchpad for hard, branching problems
mcp.post: token-heavy per call — use it for genuinely hard problems

mcp.name: Memory (knowledge graph)
mcp.description: Persistent entity/relation store the agent can write to and query across sessions

mcp.name: Fetch (URL → markdown)
mcp.description: Fetch a web page and hand it back as markdown

mcp.name: Git
mcp.description: Repository history, diffs, blame and branch operations as tools
mcp.post: overlaps the native Bash git access — add it when you want structured git tools

mcp.name: Postgres (crystaldba)
mcp.description: Schema inspection, safe SQL, EXPLAIN, index and health analysis

mcp.name: Octocode (GitHub code search)
mcp.description: Search and read code across GitHub repositories, plus npm lookups
mcp.post: authenticates via your existing `gh auth login` (or GITHUB_TOKEN)

mcp.name: Tavily (web search)
mcp.description: Web search, extract, map and crawl built for agents

mcp.name: Brave Search
mcp.description: Web, news, image and local search through the Brave API
mcp.post: requires a Brave Search API key

mcp.name: Exa
mcp.description: Neural web search and page fetch tuned for research
mcp.license: MIT (repo LICENSE; npm metadata omits it)
mcp.post: requires an Exa API key for production use

mcp.name: Firecrawl
mcp.description: Scrape, crawl and map sites into clean markdown
mcp.post: scrape/search work on the free tier; crawl/map need a key

mcp.name: Supabase
mcp.description: Project database, edge functions, logs and docs for a Supabase project

mcp.name: Neon
mcp.description: Serverless Postgres: branches, schema, queries and observability
mcp.post: append your NEON_API_KEY to args, or use the hosted OAuth endpoint

mcp.name: DeepWiki
mcp.description: Ask questions about any public GitHub repo's generated wiki (hosted, no key)
mcp.license: hosted service — Cognition/Devin terms apply (no code installed)
mcp.post: no account needed; read_wiki_contents can return very large payloads

mcp.name: Chrome DevTools
mcp.description: Performance traces, console and network with source maps — diagnosis rather than automation
mcp.post: 57 tools — heavy; add it when you are chasing a perf or runtime bug

mcp.name: Serena (symbol-level code intelligence)
mcp.description: LSP-grade symbols, references and symbol-scoped edits instead of grep-and-replace
mcp.post: needs uv; indexes the repo on first run

mcp.name: GitHub (hosted)
mcp.description: Pull requests, issues, checks and CI state for the repo you are in
mcp.license: hosted service — GitHub terms (local server: MIT)
mcp.post: OAuth on first use; 90+ tools — scope them with X-MCP-Toolsets if context gets tight

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: Root-cause-first debugging protocol (nothing in this toolkit debugs a failing L0/L1 today)
skills.install: tmp=$(mktemp -d) && git clone --depth 1 -q https://github.com/obra/superpowers "$tmp" && mkdir -p .claude/skills && cp -r "$tmp/skills/systematic-debugging" .claude/skills/ && mkdir -p .claude/licenses && cp "$tmp/LICENSE" .claude/licenses/superpowers.LICENSE 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$tmp"
